@section:console: The console's own clock and coin cell
@section:hotkey_names: Short hotkey names, used by the conflict warning
@section:link: Link cable: the button tooltip and its menu
bios: BIOS image — pick the one that boots
bios_hle_hint: Booting the emulator's own clean-room BIOS. It runs games, saves and the link cable, but not the console's boot animation or setup screens. No BIOS dump is supplied with the emulator: the two slots above read files you provide.
bios_none: No BIOS available at all — games will not reach their title screen. Point one of the slots above at a dump, or select the built-in HLE BIOS.
bios_fallback: That slot is empty, so {name} is booting instead. Fill it in to boot the console you selected.
bios_slot_ok_colour: {name} — a colour NGPC BIOS. Cartridges are told they are on an NGPC (0x6F91 = 0x10).
bios_slot_ok_mono: {name} — a monochrome NGP BIOS. Cartridges are told they are on an NGP (0x6F91 = 0x00), which is what makes games like SNK vs. Capcom show their mono screen.
bios_slot_wrong_colour: {name} looks like the MONOCHROME NGP BIOS, not a colour one. Colour games will be told they are on an NGP.
bios_slot_wrong_mono: {name} looks like the COLOUR NGPC BIOS: it stamps 0x6F91 = 0x10 and drives the K2GE colour registers, so a game would still see an NGPC. Point this slot at the monochrome NGP dump.
bios_slot_unknown: {name} — not a BIOS this emulator recognises. It will be booted as given.
cart_wait_hint: Models the slow cartridge flash bus + block-copy timing. Without it the CPU runs cart code ~3.4x too fast, so self-timed games (Cool Boarders, Densha de Go) run at 60fps instead of the 30fps a real console shows — their in-game timer then counts ~2x too fast. Fetch timing is silicon-confirmed; the LDIR block-copy part is strongly evidenced but not yet ROM-confirmed, so check the in-game timer against a stopwatch. Leave ON; turn OFF to compare with the old (too-fast) timing.
clk_paused: Stops, and resumes where it left off
clock_manual_hint: Used by the “Set by hand” mode: the console's clock starts at this date and time at every launch. On real hardware the BIOS setup screen is where you would set it — the built-in HLE BIOS has no such screen, so this is how you set the clock when running it. To set it once and then let it run, choose it here, start a game, then switch back to “Keeps running”.
clock_mode: Clock while the emulator is closed
clock_mode_hint: A real console's clock runs off its coin cell whether or not you are playing, so shutting the emulator for three days should bring it back three days later — that is the default. 'Follow the PC's clock' sets it from your computer at every launch: always right, but it overrides whatever date you set on the BIOS screen. 'Stops' freezes time with the emulator — not what hardware does, but it is reproducible, which is what you want when debugging.
coin_cell_busy: Quit the game first — the console is running.
coin_cell_confirm:
This clears the BIOS settings (language, colour) and the clock, and the console will run its first-boot setup again.

Your games and their saves are not affected.

Reset it?
coin_cell_done: Console reset — it will boot as new.
coin_cell_empty: Nothing to reset: this console has no saved settings yet.
coin_cell_hint: One battery keeps BOTH the BIOS settings (language, colour) and the clock alive. Resetting it is pulling that battery out: the console forgets its language and date and runs its first-boot setup again, exactly like a brand-new machine. Your games and their saves are NOT touched.
console_boot: Play the console boot (BIOS) before the game
console_boot_hint: Powers the console on for real: the Neo Geo Pocket BIOS plays its intro, then boots the game on its own — just like hardware. A brand-new console configures itself the first time (first-boot setup auto-completed with defaults and remembered), so you always get intro → game with no setup to click through. Leave OFF to hand the cartridge straight to the game (instant).
controls_hint: Click a button, then press the key to bind it.
cover_bad: That file could not be read as an image.
cover_failed: The cover could not be saved.
covers_need_bios: Covers are rendered by booting each game, which needs the Neo Geo Pocket BIOS. Add a bios.bin — Settings ▸ BIOS. Right-click a card to set your own cover instead.
crash_needs_bios:
⚠ This game needs the Neo Geo Pocket BIOS (not loaded).
Add a bios.bin — Settings ▸ BIOS.
filter_plugins_hint: Optional. Point this at a folder of your own holding graphics filter plugins (Scale2x, HQx, 2xSaI…) and they join the list above. None are supplied: the good scalers exist as copyleft code that an MIT-licensed emulator cannot redistribute, so it loads yours instead. One Python file per filter — the contract is three names (NAME, SCALE, apply) and is documented in the README.
filter_plugins_none: No usable filter in that folder.
gamepad_hint: Reads an Xbox-style (XInput) controller alongside the keyboard. D-pad and left stick move; A/X and B/Y are the two console buttons; Start or Back is Option. Windows only — elsewhere this does nothing.
hk_dupe: ⚠ Two hotkeys share a key: {hk}. Only the first one will fire.
hotkeys_hint: Click a hotkey, then press the key to bind it. Ctrl+1…5 always sets the window size and cannot be rebound.
key_conflict: ⚠ This key is already {hk}. In game the hotkey wins and this button will not respond.
link_btn_tip: Link / 2-player — same PC, host, or join online
mono_mode_hint: Which machine the cartridge is in. An NGPC tells every cartridge it is a colour console, and a colour-aware mono game (Samurai Shodown) then paints its own palette; a colour game asked to run on an NGP can notice and show a different screen (SNK vs. Capcom). Choose NGP to be the original hardware, in eight greys — with its own BIOS if you supplied one. Takes effect the next time a game is started.
no_roms: No ROMs found. Set your ROM folder in Settings.
pad_none: Controller support unavailable on this system
portable_hint: ON: store settings in a config.ini next to the emulator, so they travel with the folder. OFF: use the operating system's store (the Windows registry). Switching migrates your current settings across. Leave OFF if the emulator is installed in a read-only location like Program Files.
real_bios: Boot the real BIOS at power-on
turbo_hint: Holding a turbo button fires it repeatedly. The rate is counted in console frames, so it stays the same under fast-forward.
cart_lang_hint: Which language a BILINGUAL cartridge runs in (system byte 0x6F87). ⚠️ This setting is for the built-in HLE BIOS, which has no setup screen, and for a console that has never been configured. With a real BIOS the console's own setup screen owns the choice: what you set there is saved in the battery RAM and wins, in both boot modes. Use Reset the coin cell to start over. Takes effect at the next launch.

mirror_trading: 🪞 trading cartridges with the other player…

mirror_desync: 🪞 the two consoles no longer match — session ended
mirror_refused: 🪞 mirror refused: {why} must be identical on both PCs

net_pending_title: A link attempt is already running
net_pending_ask:
This console is still waiting for the other player.

Cancel that attempt?
net_err_name: that address does not resolve — check the name or IP
net_err_refused: nothing is listening on that port — has the other player clicked Host yet?
net_err_timeout_join: no answer — the host's port is closed, or a firewall/router is in the way. Without a port forward, the simplest route is a virtual private network (Tailscale, ZeroTier): both PCs land on one local network and the LAN mode is enough
net_err_timeout_host: nobody connected. Off your own network this needs a port forward on your router — or a virtual private network (Tailscale, ZeroTier), which needs none
net_err_in_use: that port is already in use on this PC — pick another, or close the other session
net_err_unreachable: that address cannot be reached from this PC — a 192.168.x / 10.x address only works on the same network. Off it you need the host's public IP WITH a port forward, or a virtual private network (Tailscale, ZeroTier) that puts both PCs back on one local network
net_err_denied: the system refused that port — Windows Firewall, or a port below 1024
link_lost: 🔌 link lost: {why} — the game keeps running
link_peer_left: the other player left the room
host_warning: ⚠️ Advanced mode. Best for people comfortable with IT security, or shared only with trusted people you know — not posted to a public list of strangers. Details below.
host_wan: • Internet: your friend dials {addr} (needs the port-forward below — and cannot be tested from this network)
host_wan_none: • Internet: could not detect a public IP (offline?)
host_help_html:
How it works — to play over the internet, your router must allow incoming connections to your PC. In its admin page (often 192.168.1.1), under Port forwarding / NAT, forward port {port} (TCP) to your PC's local IP ({lan}).

⛔ You cannot test your public address from your own network. Two PCs in the same house must use the LAN line above. Dialing your own public IP from inside usually fails even when the forward is perfectly set — most routers do not send a packet back in through their own front door (NAT hairpinning). A LAN test that works and an internet test that fails, both from home, is the EXPECTED result and says nothing: only a friend on another connection can tell you the forward works.

⚠️ The risks, straight — there are TWO levels:

1) The port itself — low risk. It only exposes this program (the emulator), not your whole PC: no login, no file access, no command execution, the game runs sandboxed. Realistic worst case: someone crashes your session.

2) Publishing your IP — the real risk. Your public IP is your online home address. Whoever has it can scan ALL your ports (not just this one) for other weak spots (router, NAS, camera…), and can DDoS / knock you offline (griefing).

➡ The rule: sharing with a trusted friend (privately) = fine. Posting to strangers = avoid — you're broadcasting your address.
➡ Good practice: only forward while playing and remove the forward after.
➡ For strangers / if unsure: a virtual private network (Tailscale, ZeroTier) or a tunnel (playit.gg) lets people reach you without exposing your IP or opening a port. With a virtual private network both PCs land on one local network, so it is the LAN line above you use then, not the public IP. The online lobby has no public server — you have to run your own (server/README.md).
lobby_server_hint: no public server is provided — give your own (see server/README.md)
lobby_connected: Connected. Create a game or join one.
lobby_hosting: Hosting room {room} — waiting for a player to join…
lobby_private_ask: Make this a PRIVATE game (password required)?
covers_regen_tip: Render every cover again. New games get a cover on their own — this is for redoing the ones you already have.
covers_regen_ask:
Render the covers of all {n} game(s) again?

Each one is booted to capture a frame, so this takes a while on a large library. Covers you chose yourself are kept.
lobby_mode_ask:
🪞 Mirror play?

Yes — mirror: both consoles run on both PCs and only the buttons cross. Full speed whatever the ping, and the only mode Card Fighters' Clash's VS match survives. Needs the same BIOS and the same build on both sides.

No — cable: the console's own link cable, relayed. Works with any build, but the game waits for the network.
settings_restored:
Your settings were missing from the system store and have been restored from the emulator's own backup ({n} restored).

The backup is kept beside the emulator as settings_backup.ini.
host_other_addrs: • Other addresses on this PC: {addrs} — a virtual private network (Tailscale, ZeroTier) shows up here, and that is the one to use to play remotely without touching your router
gif_capture_hint: Game time; pauses excluded. Raw pixels, no filters.
